scenario_description:
Objective: Add a brief hearing-comfort pouch check to an already scheduled Union Station report morning.
Emerging Need: A general concourse notice becomes useful only after the report gap, current pouch availability, and a specific no-cost seal-check card are visible.
Decision Context: Saved hearing-comfort guidance distinguishes this quick orientation from generic wellness-booth browsing; calendar, household message, and station emails define fit and timing.
Consequence: Timely organization could give Marek a better-labeled travel pouch and practical seal-check reference, while ignoring it leaves the normal shift unchanged; after release, the extra benefit is unavailable.

parameter.title: Passenger service report ORD 381
parameter.description: Confirmed Union Station report with onboard passenger-service segment and platform boarding support.

parameter.subject: June 8 concourse comfort pop-up preview
parameter.body: A passenger-crew comfort pop-up is planned for Monday morning near the south concourse. Several short demonstration cards may be released once vendors confirm staffing; topics and times are still pending.

parameter.content: I found the beige hearing-comfort pouch on the laundry shelf and set it next to your rail bag. The foam-tip sleeve and blank pocket label are both inside.

parameter.subject: One hearing-comfort seal-check card open before 11:00 reports
parameter.body: The south concourse table has one no-cost 10:10-10:20 card for a foam-tip seal check and pouch label setup. It is nonclinical, bring the current pouch, and reply by 08:30 if you want the counter to hold the card; unclaimed cards are released after that.

parameter.subject: Hearing-comfort seal-check card released
parameter.body: The 10:10 hearing-comfort card was not held by the 08:30 reply cutoff and has been released to the walk-up list. No additional cards are planned before the 11:00 report wave.
